walkthroughs.body_html:
Christianity teaches there are two kinds of sin.

Original sin: Augustine's teaching that humans inherit a sinful nature from Adam and Eve's fall.

Actual sin: the wrong acts each person freely chooses. Romans 3:23 — 'all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God'.

Christians believe Jesus will return and judge the living and the dead.

Matthew 25 — sheep and goats: those who fed the hungry and visited prisoners are welcomed; those who didn't are turned away.

The criteria combine faith in Jesus and a life of love.

Heaven = eternal life with God. Hell = eternal separation. Some view these literally; others see them as spiritual states.

Purgatory — Roman Catholic only — is a place/state of purification before heaven. Protestants reject it.

The problem of evil: Augustine said evil came from human sin and is the absence of good; Irenaeus said suffering helps souls grow.

mcqs.q: What do Christians mean by resurrection, and how does it differ from reincarnation?
options: Resurrection and reincarnation are basically the same idea of life after death.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.

Resurrection is the once-for-all bodily raising to eternal life at the end of time (modelled on Christ's resurrection); reincarnation is the soul's repeated rebirth into new bodies. They are distinct doctrines from different religious traditions.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.

mcqs.q: What is the doctrine of the Trinity?
options: God is one being existing in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) — distinct in person but united in essence; Christians remain monotheistic.
Christians believe in three different gods.
The Trinity refers to heaven, earth and hell.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.

mcqs.q: What do orthodox Christians believe about the nature of Jesus?
options: Jesus was half God and half human.
He is fully God and fully human at the same time (the incarnation) — both natures united in one person, as defined at the Council of Chalcedon.
Christians believe everyone is reincarnated until they accept Jesus.
Jesus was a human who became God after his resurrection.
